title: How TeraWulf’s Anthropic Deal Booted Up a $19B AI Empire
author: Jeffrey Neal Johnson
description: TeraWulf Inc. secured a landmark 20-year lease agreement with Anthropic worth an estimated $19 billion, transitioning from volatile cryptocurrency mining to stable, high-margin AI infrastructure hosting. The company sold its stake in the Abernathy Joint Venture for $450 million to fund the 401-megawatt Justified Data campus in Kentucky. This shift from unpredictable mining rewards (~$87,000/MW/month) to utility-grade AI workloads (~$149,000/MW/month) fundamentally improves margins and revenue visibility, while high institutional ownership and elevated short interest create potential for significant price appreciation.

title: Why AI’s Next Bottleneck May Be Power, Not Chips
author: Anna Coulling
description: Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness LP fund has doubled its equity exposure to $13.68B, positioning heavily in physical AI infrastructure and energy suppliers while hedging semiconductor exposure. The fund's thesis argues that power and electricity, not chips, represent the real bottleneck for AI scaling. The portfolio employs a barbell strategy: aggressive longs in energy infrastructure (Bloom Energy, Bitcoin miners turned AI operators) and optical components, combined with significant put hedges on semiconductor names to protect against potential sector rotation.

title: 24-Year-Old Turns $875 Million Into $2.2 Billion Via Bloom Energy Stock
author: Erica Kollmann
description: Leopold Aschenbrenner, a 24-year-old former OpenAI researcher, launched Situational Awareness LP hedge fund with $225 million based on his thesis that AI's primary constraint would be power supply. His $875 million position in Bloom Energy Corp., accumulated throughout 2025, has grown to approximately $2.21 billion as the market recognized the AI power crunch. The fund has grown to roughly $5.5 billion in about a year, with Bloom Energy shares gaining nearly 24% on Tuesday following an expanded fuel cell deal with Oracle.

title: Core Scientific Stock Up 84% as Fund Cuts Stake by $8.6 Million
author: Jonathan Ponciano
description: Kintayl Capital sold 495,390 shares of Core Scientific (CORZ) worth $8.64 million in Q4 2025, reducing its stake from 6.3% to 0.66% of AUM. Despite the fund's exit, Core Scientific shares have surged 84% over the past year. The company is transitioning from unprofitable self-mining to higher-margin colocation services, though adjusted EBITDA remains negative and Q4 revenue declined year-over-year.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the stock has appreciated 84% over the past year, the article highlights that fundamentals remain weak with declining revenue, negative adjusted EBITDA, and heavy infrastructure investments. The fund's significant stake reduction suggests the stock may have outpaced its underlying business improvements. The company's transition toward colocation is positive long-term, but execution remains uncertain.
